citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1001. Organization of council, quorum, participation by telecommunication device, voting, compensation and eligibility (2023)
content:
(a) Organization.--The council shall organize on the first Monday of January of each even-numbered year
      by electing one member as president and one member as vice president, who shall hold
      the offices at the pleasure of the council.  If the first Monday is a legal holiday, the meeting and organization shall take
      place the following day.  Any action taken by any council at any time between 12:01 a.m. on January 1 of an
      even-numbered year and the organization of council in that year shall be subject to
      reconsideration by the new council at any time within ten days after organization.  The council may, at the organizational meeting, appoint other officers as may be
      provided for by law or ordinance, or as may be deemed necessary for the conduct of
      affairs of the borough, and may transact any other business as may come before the
      meeting.  The president, and, during the president's absence or incapacity, the vice president,
      shall preside over the meetings of council and perform other duties as are prescribed
      by this part or by ordinance.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1003. When the mayor may preside over council and vote, attendance of mayor at council meetings and breaking tie votes (2023)
content:
(a) Presiding over meetings.--The mayor shall preside over the organization of the council until it is organized
      as provided in section 1001 (relating to organization of council, quorum, participation
      by telecommunication device, voting, compensation and eligibility) and shall be deemed
      a member of council at the organizational meeting if the mayor's membership becomes
      necessary to constitute a quorum.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1053. Compensation of auditors (2023)
content:
(a) General compensation.--Subject to the limitations set forth in subsection (b), each auditor shall receive
      $10 per hour for each hour or portion of an hour necessarily employed in the discharge
      of the auditor's duties, to be paid by the borough.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1055. Subpoenas, oath and perjury
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1055. Subpoenas, oath and perjury
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1055. Subpoenas, oath and perjury (2023)
content:
(a) Subpoenas.--A majority of the auditors of any borough shall have the power to issue subpoenas
      to obtain the attendance of the persons whose accounts they are required to adjust,
      their executors and administrators, and of any persons whom it may be necessary to
      examine as witnesses and to compel their attendance, and may also compel the production
      of all documents, including books, vouchers and papers relative to borough accounts.  If any person refuses or neglects to appear, to produce documents or to testify,
      the auditors shall petition the court of common pleas of the county to issue a subpoena
      to the person and to require the person to produce documents or to appear and to testify
      before the court.  The court shall issue the subpoena if it deems the documents or testimony relevant
      to the issue.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter A. Council›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1016. Examination of witnesses; penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter A. Council › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1016. Examination of witnesses; penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1016. Examination of witnesses; penalty (2023)
content:
An individual called as a witness, as provided in this chapter, may be examined under
   oath, administered by the president of council or chair of the committee and, for
   the giving of false testimony, shall be liable for prosecution under applicable laws
   for perjury.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1041. Auditors to meet yearly and audit accounts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1041. Auditors to meet yearly and audit accounts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1041. Auditors to meet yearly and audit accounts (2023)
content:
(a) First meeting.--The auditors of the borough shall meet on the first Tuesday of January of each year
      and shall organize by the election of a chair and a secretary.  If the first Tuesday is a legal holiday, the meeting and organization shall take
      place the following day.  Two auditors shall constitute a quorum.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter A. Council›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1015. Witness fees and mileage
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter A. Council › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1015. Witness fees and mileage
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1015. Witness fees and mileage (2023)
content:
No individual residing outside the borough and subpoenaed under section 1014 (relating
   to hearings before council;  witnesses) shall be required to respond to the subpoena
   until mileage to and from the borough at the rate established by the council under
   the act of July 20, 1979 (P.L. 156, No. 51),1referred to as the Uniform Mileage Fee Law, and witness fees as required by law relating
   to witnesses have been paid.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter A. Council›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1014. Hearings before council; witnesses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter A. Council › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1014. Hearings before council; witnesses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1014. Hearings before council; witnesses (2023)
content:
Councils may compel the attendance of witnesses and the production of books, papers
   or other evidence at any meeting of the council or any committee of the council and
   for that purpose may issue subpoenas, signed by the president of council or the chair
   of the committee, which shall be served in any part of this Commonwealth.  If a witness refuses to testify to any fact within the witness's knowledge or to
   produce any books or papers in the witness's possession or control required to be
   used as evidence in any case, the borough solicitor shall report the facts relating
   to the refusal to the court of common pleas.  If the court determines the evidence required of the witness to be legal and competent,
   it shall order the witness to testify or produce the evidence required.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter A. Council›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1004. Failure of council to organize
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter A. Council › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1004. Failure of council to organize
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1004. Failure of council to organize (2023)
content:
If the council of any borough fails to organize within ten days from the time prescribed
   in this chapter, the court of common pleas, upon the petition of at least ten registered
   electors of the borough verified by the affidavit of one of the petitioners, shall
   issue a rule upon the delinquent members of council to show cause why their seats
   should not be declared vacant.  The rule shall be returnable not less than five days from the time of its issue,
   and, after hearing, the court may declare the seats of the members of council responsible
   for the failure to organize vacant and shall appoint others in their place, who shall
   hold office for the respective unexpired terms.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1058. Pay of witnesses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1058. Pay of witnesses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1058. Pay of witnesses (2023)
content:
Witnesses, other than officers of the borough, appearing before the auditors and individuals
   or officers serving subpoenas shall be paid, out of the borough treasury upon authorization
   signed by a majority of the auditors and orders drawn on the borough treasury, the
   same fees as are payable for rendering similar services in civil proceedings before
   a magisterial district judge.  The amount paid shall be made a part of the charge against any officer who shall
   be charged by the auditors with any balance, if the costs have been incurred in establishing
   the balance.  The costs collected from any officer shall be repaid into the borough treasury.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.3. Surcharge by auditors (2023)
content: (a) Surcharges.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059. Auditors to settle accounts where witnesses do not appear
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059. Auditors to settle accounts where witnesses do not appear
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059. Auditors to settle accounts where witnesses do not appear (2023)
content:
If any person in possession of documents relative to public accounts before auditors
   refuses to produce the same or if any officer whose accounts are to be settled and
   adjusted by the auditors refuses to appear or submit to examination as directed by
   this subchapter, the auditors or a majority of them may proceed, by the examination
   of witnesses and other evidence, to ascertain and settle, as near as may be, the amount
   of public money received by the officer and its application to public purposes or
   otherwise.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.1. Completion, filing and publication of auditor's report and financial statement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.1. Completion, filing and publication of auditor's report and financial statement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.1. Completion, filing and publication of auditor's report and financial statement (2023)
content:
(a) Report.--The auditors shall complete the annual audit, adjustment and settlement as soon as
      possible after the end of the fiscal year.  The auditors shall, within ten days after completing the annual audit, publish once,
      in at least one newspaper of general circulation, concise financial information prepared
      or approved by the auditors and consistent with the audited financial statements for
      total assets, total liabilities and total net position at the end of the fiscal year
      and total revenue, total expenses and changes in total net position for that fiscal
      year and a reference to a place within the borough where copies of the financial statements
      and accompanying audit report may be examined.  If the full financial statements and accompanying audit report are not published,
      copies shall be supplied to the publishing newspaper when the request for publication
      is submitted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.5. Taxpayers appealing to enter bond
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.5. Taxpayers appealing to enter bond
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.5. Taxpayers appealing to enter bond (2023)
content:
No appeal by a taxpayer or officer may be allowed unless, within the time of taking
   the appeal, the appellant secures a bond in the sum of $1,000 with sufficient surety
   to prosecute the appeal and to pay all costs of appeal, in case, if the appellant
   is a taxpayer, the appellant fails to obtain a final decision more favorable to the
   borough than that awarded by the auditors or, in case, if the appellant is an accounting
   officer, the appellant fails to obtain a final decision more favorable to the officer
   than that awarded by the auditors.  Unless the bond is filed as provided in this section, the court of common pleas,
   upon application, shall set aside the appeal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter A. Council›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1009. Typewritten, printed, photocopied, microfilmed and electronically or digitally stored records valid and recording or transcribing records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter A. Council › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1009. Typewritten, printed, photocopied, microfilmed and electronically or digitally stored records valid and recording or transcribing records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1009. Typewritten, printed, photocopied, microfilmed and electronically or digitally stored records valid and recording or transcribing records (2023)
content:
(a) Validity.--All borough records required to be recorded or transcribed shall be deemed valid if
      typewritten, printed, photocopied, microfilmed or electronically or digitally stored
      or retained by any other process that accurately reproduces the original and forms
      a durable medium for recording, storing and reproducing in accordance with the act
      of May 9, 1949 (P.L. 908, No. 250),1entitled “An act relating to public records of political subdivisions other than
      cities and counties of the first class;  authorizing the recording and copying of
      documents, plats, papers and instruments of writing by digital, photostatic, photographic,
      microfilm or other process, and the admissibility and enlargements in evidence;  providing
      for the storage of duplicates and sale of microfilm and digital copies of official
      records and for the destruction of other records deemed valueless;  and providing
      for the services of the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission to political
      subdivisions.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.2. Attorney to auditors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.2. Attorney to auditors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.2. Attorney to auditors (2023)
content:
The borough auditors may employ an attorney if deemed advisable by a majority of the
   auditors.  The auditors, with the agreement of council, shall determine the compensation to
   be paid to the attorney.  If the auditors and council cannot agree on the compensation, upon petition of the
   auditors, the court of common pleas shall establish the compensation for the attorney
   employed by the auditors.  The compensation for the attorney shall be paid out of the borough general fund.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.6. Procedure on appeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.6. Procedure on appeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.6. Procedure on appeals (2023)
content:
(a) Evidence and burden.--In any proceeding upon an appeal from a report of the auditors, the accounts of the
      office or officers or the person, corporation, association, organization, committee
      or commission in question may be investigated de novo, and the burden shall be upon
      each officer, person, corporation, association, organization, committee or commission
      whose accounts are involved in the appeal of establishing the person's right to credits
      claimed by the person, but the opposing party in the appeal may use any facts, figures
      or findings of the report of the auditors as prima facie evidence against any officer
      or other entity.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.9. Balances due to be entered as judgments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.9. Balances due to be entered as judgments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.9. Balances due to be entered as judgments (2023)
content:
A balance in a report of the auditors against an officer of the borough shall constitute
   a surcharge against the officer as fully as if expressly stated in the report to be
   a surcharge.  The amount of a balance and of any express surcharge shall, if no appeal is taken
   or after an appeal has been finally determined in favor of the borough, be entered
   by the prothonotary as a judgment against the officer.  The clerk of the court of common pleas shall certify the amount of every balance
   or surcharge contained in a report from which no appeal has been taken within the
   time provided under this chapter to the court of common pleas for entry by the prothonotary
   as a judgment.  Any taxpayer of the borough may enforce the collection of the balance or surcharge
   for the benefit of the borough, by action or execution, upon filing in the court of
   common pleas a bond, in the sum of $1,000 with one or more sureties, conditioned to
   indemnify the borough from all costs of the proceedings undertaken by the taxpayer,
   subject to all rights of appeal from the report of auditors granted by this part.  If a person has been or shall be surcharged for an illegal purchase and no fraud
   or collusion is shown and the surcharge is paid to the borough, the article purchased
   shall become the property of the person surcharged.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.11. General powers and duties of independent auditor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.11. General powers and duties of independent auditor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.11. General powers and duties of independent auditor (2023)
content:
(a) Powers and duties.--If an independent auditor is appointed under section 1005(7) (relating to powers of
      council), the independent auditor shall have the same powers and duties and be subject
      to the same penalties as the auditors under this chapter.  The independent auditor shall annually examine, audit and settle all accounts in
      which the borough is concerned.  The audit shall consist of an examination in accordance with generally accepted
      auditing standards and shall include tests of the accounting records and other auditing
      procedures as the independent auditor considers necessary in the circumstances.  The independent auditor shall make and publish the annual financial report in the
      same form and manner and at the same time as required in this part of the auditors
      of the borough.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.4. Appeals from audit
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.4. Appeals from audit
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.4. Appeals from audit (2023)
content:
It shall be lawful for the borough, or any taxpayer of the borough on its behalf,
   or any person whose account is settled or audited, to appeal from the settlement or
   audit, as shown in the auditors report, to the court of common pleas of the county
   no later than 40 days from the date of the filing of the auditor's report with the
   clerk of common pleas.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1061. Oath and bond of controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1061. Oath and bond of controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1061. Oath and bond of controller (2023)
content:
The borough controller shall, before entering upon the duties of office, take the
   required oath or affirmation of office under53 Pa.C.S. § 1141(relating to form of oaths of office).  The controller shall give bond to the borough with a surety company to be approved
   by the council, in a sum as council may direct by ordinance, conditioned for the faithful
   discharge of the controller's duties.  The amount of the bond shall be sufficient to adequately protect the borough from
   any illegal or unfaithful action by the controller.  The cost of the bond shall be paid by the borough.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.7. Findings of fact and law, judgment and appeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.7. Findings of fact and law, judgment and appeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.7. Findings of fact and law, judgment and appeals (2023)
content:
After the hearing, the court shall file its findings of fact and law and enter judgment
   accordingly, and the judgment so entered may be enforced by the prevailing party by
   any appropriate proceeding.  Appeals from the court's ruling may be taken in accordance with law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1063. General powers and duties of controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1063. General powers and duties of controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1063. General powers and duties of controller (2023)
content:
(a) General duties and powers.--The borough controller shall manage the fiscal affairs of the borough.  The controller shall examine, audit and settle all accounts in which the borough
      is concerned either as debtor or creditor if provision for the settlement is made
      by law.  If no provision or an insufficient provision has been made, the controller shall
      examine the accounts and report to the council the relevant facts and opinion on the
      accounts.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1070. Appeals from controller's report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1070. Appeals from controller's report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1070. Appeals from controller's report (2023)
content:
Appeals may be taken from the settlement and audit of the controller, as shown in
   the controller's report to the court of common pleas of the county, by the same persons
   in the same manner within the same time subject to the same conditions and procedure
   and with like effect in every respect as provided in this part in the cases of appeals
   from the settlement and audit of the auditors as shown in their report.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1065. Countersigned warrants
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1065. Countersigned warrants
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1065. Countersigned warrants (2023)
content:
The controller shall countersign all warrants upon the borough treasurer, with the
   form of the warrant to be prescribed by council, except that no warrant shall be countersigned
   unless there is money in the treasury to pay the warrant.  If a warrant on the treasurer shall be presented to the controller to be countersigned,
   the person presenting the warrant shall, if the controller requires, produce evidence
   that:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.10. Penalty for failure to comply with law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.10. Penalty for failure to comply with law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.10. Penalty for failure to comply with law (2023)
content: (a) Neglect.--An auditor neglecting or refusing to comply with this chapter commits a summary offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1069. Books to be kept by controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1069. Books to be kept by controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1069. Books to be kept by controller (2023)
content:
The borough controller shall keep a regular set of books which shall be opened and
   keep as many accounts, under appropriate titles, as may be necessary to show separately
   and distinctly all the estates and property, real and personal, vested in the borough,
   all trusts in the care of the borough, all debts due and owing the borough, all receipts
   and expenditures of the various departments of the borough government and all appropriations
   made by council and the sums under the same, respectively.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1068. Controller's recommendations on borough finances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1068. Controller's recommendations on borough finances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1068. Controller's recommendations on borough finances (2023)
content:
The borough controller shall, as often as the controller may deem expedient or the
   council shall direct, suggest plans to the council for the management and improvement
   of the borough finances.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1067. Amount of contracts to be charged against appropriations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1067. Amount of contracts to be charged against appropriations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1067. Amount of contracts to be charged against appropriations (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A contract involving appropriation of money shall designate the item of appropriation
      on which it is founded, and the estimated amount of the expenditure which shall be
      charged against the item, and certified by the borough controller on the contract,
      before it shall take effect as a contract.  Payment required by the contract shall be made from the fund appropriated.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1066. Prevention of appropriation overdrafts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1066. Prevention of appropriation overdrafts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1066. Prevention of appropriation overdrafts (2023)
content:
The controller shall not permit any appropriation made by the council to be overdrawn.  If an appropriation is exhausted, the object of which is not complete, the controller
   shall immediately report the fact to the council and accompany the report with a statement
   of the money which has been drawn on the appropriation and the particular purpose
   for which it is drawn.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter F. Tax Collector›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1086. Powers and duties of tax collector
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter F. Tax Collector › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1086. Powers and duties of tax collector
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1086. Powers and duties of tax collector (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (b), the tax collector shall be the collector
      of all State, county, borough, school, institution district and other taxes levied
      within the borough by the authorities empowered to levy taxes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1071. Acceptance by ordinance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1071. Acceptance by ordinance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1071. Acceptance by ordinance (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--This subchapter shall not become operative or effective in any borough not having
      a controller until the borough shall, by ordinance, accept this chapter.  If a borough accepts this subchapter, the court of common pleas, upon petition of
      council, shall appoint a controller to hold office until the first Monday of January
      following the next municipal election at which a controller shall be elected under
      this part.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter A. Council›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1002. Oath of members of council
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter A. Council › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1002. Oath of members of council
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1002. Oath of members of council (2023)
content:
Before entering upon the duties of their offices, the members of council shall take
   and subscribe an oath or affirmation of office under53 Pa.C.S. § 1141(relating to form of oaths of office).  The oath or affirmation may be taken before any judge or magisterial district judge
   of the county, a notary public or the mayor of the borough when the individual has
   qualified, and the oath or affirmation shall be filed with the borough secretary and
   preserved among the records of the borough for a period of six years.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter A. Council›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1001. Organization of council, quorum, participation by telecommunication device, voting, compensation and eligibility
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter A. Council › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1001. Organization of council, quorum, participation by telecommunication device, voting, compensation and eligibility
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1001. Organization of council, quorum, participation by telecommunication device, voting, compensation and eligibility (2023)
content:
(a) Organization.--The council shall organize on the first Monday of January of each even-numbered year
      by electing one member as president and one member as vice president, who shall hold
      the offices at the pleasure of the council.  If the first Monday is a legal holiday, the meeting and organization shall take
      place the following day.  Any action taken by any council at any time between 12:01 a.m. on January 1 of an
      even-numbered year and the organization of council in that year shall be subject to
      reconsideration by the new council at any time within ten days after organization.  The council may, at the organizational meeting, appoint other officers as may be
      provided for by law or ordinance, or as may be deemed necessary for the conduct of
      affairs of the borough, and may transact any other business as may come before the
      meeting.  The president, and, during the president's absence or incapacity, the vice president,
      shall preside over the meetings of council and perform other duties as are prescribed
      by this part or by ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1062. Salary of controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10. Powers and Duties of Elected Officials › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1062. Salary of controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1062. Salary of controller (2023)
content:
The council shall fix the annual salary of the controller.  Any change in salary, compensation or emoluments of the elected office shall become
   effective at the beginning of the next term of the controller.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter A. Council›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1015. Witness fees and mileage
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter A. Council › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1015. Witness fees and mileage
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1015. Witness fees and mileage (2023)
content:
No individual residing outside the borough and subpoenaed under section 1014 (relating
   to hearings before council;  witnesses) shall be required to respond to the subpoena
   until mileage to and from the borough at the rate established by the council under
   the act of July 20, 1979 (P.L. 156, No. 51),1referred to as the Uniform Mileage Fee Law, and witness fees as required by law relating
   to witnesses have been paid.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter A. Council›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1003. When the mayor may preside over council and vote, attendance of mayor at council meetings and breaking tie votes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter A. Council › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1003. When the mayor may preside over council and vote, attendance of mayor at council meetings and breaking tie votes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1003. When the mayor may preside over council and vote, attendance of mayor at council meetings and breaking tie votes (2023)
content:
(a) Presiding over meetings.--The mayor shall preside over the organization of the council until it is organized
      as provided in section 1001 (relating to organization of council, quorum, participation
      by telecommunication device, voting, compensation and eligibility) and shall be deemed
      a member of council at the organizational meeting if the mayor's membership becomes
      necessary to constitute a quorum.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter A. Council›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1016. Examination of witnesses; penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter A. Council › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1016. Examination of witnesses; penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1016. Examination of witnesses; penalty (2023)
content:
An individual called as a witness, as provided in this chapter, may be examined under
   oath, administered by the president of council or chair of the committee and, for
   the giving of false testimony, shall be liable for prosecution under applicable laws
   for perjury.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter A. Council›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1009. Typewritten, printed, photocopied, microfilmed and electronically or digitally stored records valid and recording or transcribing records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter A. Council › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1009. Typewritten, printed, photocopied, microfilmed and electronically or digitally stored records valid and recording or transcribing records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1009. Typewritten, printed, photocopied, microfilmed and electronically or digitally stored records valid and recording or transcribing records (2023)
content:
(a) Validity.--All borough records required to be recorded or transcribed shall be deemed valid if
      typewritten, printed, photocopied, microfilmed or electronically or digitally stored
      or retained by any other process that accurately reproduces the original and forms
      a durable medium for recording, storing and reproducing in accordance with the act
      of May 9, 1949 (P.L. 908, No. 250),1entitled “An act relating to public records of political subdivisions other than
      cities and counties of the first class;  authorizing the recording and copying of
      documents, plats, papers and instruments of writing by digital, photostatic, photographic,
      microfilm or other process, and the admissibility and enlargements in evidence;  providing
      for the storage of duplicates and sale of microfilm and digital copies of official
      records and for the destruction of other records deemed valueless;  and providing
      for the services of the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission to political
      subdivisions.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter A. Council›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1004. Failure of council to organize
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter A. Council › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1004. Failure of council to organize
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1004. Failure of council to organize (2023)
content:
If the council of any borough fails to organize within ten days from the time prescribed
   in this chapter, the court of common pleas, upon the petition of at least ten registered
   electors of the borough verified by the affidavit of one of the petitioners, shall
   issue a rule upon the delinquent members of council to show cause why their seats
   should not be declared vacant.  The rule shall be returnable not less than five days from the time of its issue,
   and, after hearing, the court may declare the seats of the members of council responsible
   for the failure to organize vacant and shall appoint others in their place, who shall
   hold office for the respective unexpired terms.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1041. Auditors to meet yearly and audit accounts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1041. Auditors to meet yearly and audit accounts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1041. Auditors to meet yearly and audit accounts (2023)
content:
(a) First meeting.--The auditors of the borough shall meet on the first Tuesday of January of each year
      and shall organize by the election of a chair and a secretary.  If the first Tuesday is a legal holiday, the meeting and organization shall take
      place the following day.  Two auditors shall constitute a quorum.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059. Auditors to settle accounts where witnesses do not appear
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059. Auditors to settle accounts where witnesses do not appear
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059. Auditors to settle accounts where witnesses do not appear (2023)
content:
If any person in possession of documents relative to public accounts before auditors
   refuses to produce the same or if any officer whose accounts are to be settled and
   adjusted by the auditors refuses to appear or submit to examination as directed by
   this subchapter, the auditors or a majority of them may proceed, by the examination
   of witnesses and other evidence, to ascertain and settle, as near as may be, the amount
   of public money received by the officer and its application to public purposes or
   otherwise.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1055. Subpoenas, oath and perjury
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1055. Subpoenas, oath and perjury
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1055. Subpoenas, oath and perjury (2023)
content:
(a) Subpoenas.--A majority of the auditors of any borough shall have the power to issue subpoenas
      to obtain the attendance of the persons whose accounts they are required to adjust,
      their executors and administrators, and of any persons whom it may be necessary to
      examine as witnesses and to compel their attendance, and may also compel the production
      of all documents, including books, vouchers and papers relative to borough accounts.  If any person refuses or neglects to appear, to produce documents or to testify,
      the auditors shall petition the court of common pleas of the county to issue a subpoena
      to the person and to require the person to produce documents or to appear and to testify
      before the court.  The court shall issue the subpoena if it deems the documents or testimony relevant
      to the issue.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1053. Compensation of auditors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1053. Compensation of auditors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1053. Compensation of auditors (2023)
content:
(a) General compensation.--Subject to the limitations set forth in subsection (b), each auditor shall receive
      $10 per hour for each hour or portion of an hour necessarily employed in the discharge
      of the auditor's duties, to be paid by the borough.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.4. Appeals from audit
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.4. Appeals from audit
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.4. Appeals from audit (2023)
content:
It shall be lawful for the borough, or any taxpayer of the borough on its behalf,
   or any person whose account is settled or audited, to appeal from the settlement or
   audit, as shown in the auditors report, to the court of common pleas of the county
   no later than 40 days from the date of the filing of the auditor's report with the
   clerk of common pleas.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.1. Completion, filing and publication of auditor's report and financial statement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.1. Completion, filing and publication of auditor's report and financial statement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.1. Completion, filing and publication of auditor's report and financial statement (2023)
content:
(a) Report.--The auditors shall complete the annual audit, adjustment and settlement as soon as
      possible after the end of the fiscal year.  The auditors shall, within ten days after completing the annual audit, publish once,
      in at least one newspaper of general circulation, concise financial information prepared
      or approved by the auditors and consistent with the audited financial statements for
      total assets, total liabilities and total net position at the end of the fiscal year
      and total revenue, total expenses and changes in total net position for that fiscal
      year and a reference to a place within the borough where copies of the financial statements
      and accompanying audit report may be examined.  If the full financial statements and accompanying audit report are not published,
      copies shall be supplied to the publishing newspaper when the request for publication
      is submitted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.2. Attorney to auditors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.2. Attorney to auditors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.2. Attorney to auditors (2023)
content:
The borough auditors may employ an attorney if deemed advisable by a majority of the
   auditors.  The auditors, with the agreement of council, shall determine the compensation to
   be paid to the attorney.  If the auditors and council cannot agree on the compensation, upon petition of the
   auditors, the court of common pleas shall establish the compensation for the attorney
   employed by the auditors.  The compensation for the attorney shall be paid out of the borough general fund.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter A. Council›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1014. Hearings before council; witnesses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter A. Council › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1014. Hearings before council; witnesses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1014. Hearings before council; witnesses (2023)
content:
Councils may compel the attendance of witnesses and the production of books, papers
   or other evidence at any meeting of the council or any committee of the council and
   for that purpose may issue subpoenas, signed by the president of council or the chair
   of the committee, which shall be served in any part of this Commonwealth.  If a witness refuses to testify to any fact within the witness's knowledge or to
   produce any books or papers in the witness's possession or control required to be
   used as evidence in any case, the borough solicitor shall report the facts relating
   to the refusal to the court of common pleas.  If the court determines the evidence required of the witness to be legal and competent,
   it shall order the witness to testify or produce the evidence required.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.7. Findings of fact and law, judgment and appeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.7. Findings of fact and law, judgment and appeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.7. Findings of fact and law, judgment and appeals (2023)
content:
After the hearing, the court shall file its findings of fact and law and enter judgment
   accordingly, and the judgment so entered may be enforced by the prevailing party by
   any appropriate proceeding.  Appeals from the court's ruling may be taken in accordance with law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1058. Pay of witnesses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1058. Pay of witnesses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1058. Pay of witnesses (2023)
content:
Witnesses, other than officers of the borough, appearing before the auditors and individuals
   or officers serving subpoenas shall be paid, out of the borough treasury upon authorization
   signed by a majority of the auditors and orders drawn on the borough treasury, the
   same fees as are payable for rendering similar services in civil proceedings before
   a magisterial district judge.  The amount paid shall be made a part of the charge against any officer who shall
   be charged by the auditors with any balance, if the costs have been incurred in establishing
   the balance.  The costs collected from any officer shall be repaid into the borough treasury.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.6. Procedure on appeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.6. Procedure on appeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.6. Procedure on appeals (2023)
content:
(a) Evidence and burden.--In any proceeding upon an appeal from a report of the auditors, the accounts of the
      office or officers or the person, corporation, association, organization, committee
      or commission in question may be investigated de novo, and the burden shall be upon
      each officer, person, corporation, association, organization, committee or commission
      whose accounts are involved in the appeal of establishing the person's right to credits
      claimed by the person, but the opposing party in the appeal may use any facts, figures
      or findings of the report of the auditors as prima facie evidence against any officer
      or other entity.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1063. General powers and duties of controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1063. General powers and duties of controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1063. General powers and duties of controller (2023)
content:
(a) General duties and powers.--The borough controller shall manage the fiscal affairs of the borough.  The controller shall examine, audit and settle all accounts in which the borough
      is concerned either as debtor or creditor if provision for the settlement is made
      by law.  If no provision or an insufficient provision has been made, the controller shall
      examine the accounts and report to the council the relevant facts and opinion on the
      accounts.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.10. Penalty for failure to comply with law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.10. Penalty for failure to comply with law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.10. Penalty for failure to comply with law (2023)
content: (a) Neglect.--An auditor neglecting or refusing to comply with this chapter commits a summary offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.9. Balances due to be entered as judgments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.9. Balances due to be entered as judgments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.9. Balances due to be entered as judgments (2023)
content:
A balance in a report of the auditors against an officer of the borough shall constitute
   a surcharge against the officer as fully as if expressly stated in the report to be
   a surcharge.  The amount of a balance and of any express surcharge shall, if no appeal is taken
   or after an appeal has been finally determined in favor of the borough, be entered
   by the prothonotary as a judgment against the officer.  The clerk of the court of common pleas shall certify the amount of every balance
   or surcharge contained in a report from which no appeal has been taken within the
   time provided under this chapter to the court of common pleas for entry by the prothonotary
   as a judgment.  Any taxpayer of the borough may enforce the collection of the balance or surcharge
   for the benefit of the borough, by action or execution, upon filing in the court of
   common pleas a bond, in the sum of $1,000 with one or more sureties, conditioned to
   indemnify the borough from all costs of the proceedings undertaken by the taxpayer,
   subject to all rights of appeal from the report of auditors granted by this part.  If a person has been or shall be surcharged for an illegal purchase and no fraud
   or collusion is shown and the surcharge is paid to the borough, the article purchased
   shall become the property of the person surcharged.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.11. General powers and duties of independent auditor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.11. General powers and duties of independent auditor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.11. General powers and duties of independent auditor (2023)
content:
(a) Powers and duties.--If an independent auditor is appointed under section 1005(7) (relating to powers of
      council), the independent auditor shall have the same powers and duties and be subject
      to the same penalties as the auditors under this chapter.  The independent auditor shall annually examine, audit and settle all accounts in
      which the borough is concerned.  The audit shall consist of an examination in accordance with generally accepted
      auditing standards and shall include tests of the accounting records and other auditing
      procedures as the independent auditor considers necessary in the circumstances.  The independent auditor shall make and publish the annual financial report in the
      same form and manner and at the same time as required in this part of the auditors
      of the borough.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1062. Salary of controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1062. Salary of controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1062. Salary of controller (2023)
content:
The council shall fix the annual salary of the controller.  Any change in salary, compensation or emoluments of the elected office shall become
   effective at the beginning of the next term of the controller.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1065. Countersigned warrants
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1065. Countersigned warrants
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1065. Countersigned warrants (2023)
content:
The controller shall countersign all warrants upon the borough treasurer, with the
   form of the warrant to be prescribed by council, except that no warrant shall be countersigned
   unless there is money in the treasury to pay the warrant.  If a warrant on the treasurer shall be presented to the controller to be countersigned,
   the person presenting the warrant shall, if the controller requires, produce evidence
   that:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1066. Prevention of appropriation overdrafts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1066. Prevention of appropriation overdrafts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1066. Prevention of appropriation overdrafts (2023)
content:
The controller shall not permit any appropriation made by the council to be overdrawn.  If an appropriation is exhausted, the object of which is not complete, the controller
   shall immediately report the fact to the council and accompany the report with a statement
   of the money which has been drawn on the appropriation and the particular purpose
   for which it is drawn.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1061. Oath and bond of controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1061. Oath and bond of controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1061. Oath and bond of controller (2023)
content:
The borough controller shall, before entering upon the duties of office, take the
   required oath or affirmation of office under53 Pa.C.S. § 1141(relating to form of oaths of office).  The controller shall give bond to the borough with a surety company to be approved
   by the council, in a sum as council may direct by ordinance, conditioned for the faithful
   discharge of the controller's duties.  The amount of the bond shall be sufficient to adequately protect the borough from
   any illegal or unfaithful action by the controller.  The cost of the bond shall be paid by the borough.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1069. Books to be kept by controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1069. Books to be kept by controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1069. Books to be kept by controller (2023)
content:
The borough controller shall keep a regular set of books which shall be opened and
   keep as many accounts, under appropriate titles, as may be necessary to show separately
   and distinctly all the estates and property, real and personal, vested in the borough,
   all trusts in the care of the borough, all debts due and owing the borough, all receipts
   and expenditures of the various departments of the borough government and all appropriations
   made by council and the sums under the same, respectively.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1071. Acceptance by ordinance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1071. Acceptance by ordinance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1071. Acceptance by ordinance (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--This subchapter shall not become operative or effective in any borough not having
      a controller until the borough shall, by ordinance, accept this chapter.  If a borough accepts this subchapter, the court of common pleas, upon petition of
      council, shall appoint a controller to hold office until the first Monday of January
      following the next municipal election at which a controller shall be elected under
      this part.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1067. Amount of contracts to be charged against appropriations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1067. Amount of contracts to be charged against appropriations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1067. Amount of contracts to be charged against appropriations (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A contract involving appropriation of money shall designate the item of appropriation
      on which it is founded, and the estimated amount of the expenditure which shall be
      charged against the item, and certified by the borough controller on the contract,
      before it shall take effect as a contract.  Payment required by the contract shall be made from the fund appropriated.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.5. Taxpayers appealing to enter bond
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.5. Taxpayers appealing to enter bond
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.5. Taxpayers appealing to enter bond (2023)
content:
No appeal by a taxpayer or officer may be allowed unless, within the time of taking
   the appeal, the appellant secures a bond in the sum of $1,000 with sufficient surety
   to prosecute the appeal and to pay all costs of appeal, in case, if the appellant
   is a taxpayer, the appellant fails to obtain a final decision more favorable to the
   borough than that awarded by the auditors or, in case, if the appellant is an accounting
   officer, the appellant fails to obtain a final decision more favorable to the officer
   than that awarded by the auditors.  Unless the bond is filed as provided in this section, the court of common pleas,
   upon application, shall set aside the appeal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1068. Controller's recommendations on borough finances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1068. Controller's recommendations on borough finances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1068. Controller's recommendations on borough finances (2023)
content:
The borough controller shall, as often as the controller may deem expedient or the
   council shall direct, suggest plans to the council for the management and improvement
   of the borough finances.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Auditors›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.8. Attorney fees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Auditors › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.8. Attorney fees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1059.8. Attorney fees (2023)

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter D. Controller›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1070. Appeals from controller's report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter D. Controller › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1070. Appeals from controller's report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1070. Appeals from controller's report (2023)
content:
Appeals may be taken from the settlement and audit of the controller, as shown in
   the controller's report to the court of common pleas of the county, by the same persons
   in the same manner within the same time subject to the same conditions and procedure
   and with like effect in every respect as provided in this part in the cases of appeals
   from the settlement and audit of the auditors as shown in their report.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10A. Mayor›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A05. Salaried mayor not to receive certain fees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10A. Mayor › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A05. Salaried mayor not to receive certain fees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A05. Salaried mayor not to receive certain fees (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as provided in subsection (b), any salary paid under an ordinance shall be
      in lieu of all costs and fees allowed by a mayor.  Costs and fees shall be collected by the mayor and deposited into the borough treasury.
