path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter F. Tax Collector›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1086. Powers and duties of tax collector
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter F. Tax Collector › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1086. Powers and duties of tax collector
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1086. Powers and duties of tax collector (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (b), the tax collector shall be the collector
      of all State, county, borough, school, institution district and other taxes levied
      within the borough by the authorities empowered to levy taxes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10A. Mayor›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A06. General powers of mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10A. Mayor › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A06. General powers of mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A06. General powers of mayor (2023)
content: (a) Oaths and affirmations.--The mayor may administer oaths and affirmations in matters pertaining to borough affairs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10A. Mayor›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A02. Incompatible offices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10A. Mayor › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A02. Incompatible offices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A02. Incompatible offices (2023)
content:
No member of Congress or any person holding any office or appointment of profit or
   trust under the Federal Government or any person holding the office of magisterial
   district judge may at the same time be capable of holding the office of mayor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10A. Mayor›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A03. Oath of mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10A. Mayor › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A03. Oath of mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A03. Oath of mayor (2023)
content:
The mayor, before exercising the duties of office, shall take and subscribe an oath
   or affirmation of office under53 Pa.C.S. § 1141(relating to form of oaths of office).  The oath or affirmation may be taken before a judge or magisterial district judge
   of the county or a notary public and shall be filed with the borough secretary and
   be preserved among the records of the borough for a period of six years.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10A. Mayor›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A04. Salary of mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10A. Mayor › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A04. Salary of mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A04. Salary of mayor (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The salary of the mayor shall be established by ordinance and shall not exceed the
      following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Compensation, hours and days of work and outside employment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Compensation, hours and days of work and outside employment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Compensation, hours and days of work and outside employment (2023)
content:
Appointed officers and employees of the borough shall receive compensation for their
   services as the council shall prescribe.  Council may also establish the hours and days of work and may restrict the outside
   employment of borough employees or any class or category of employment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Appointments and incompatible offices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Appointments and incompatible offices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Appointments and incompatible offices (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Unless there is incompatibility in fact, an elective or appointive officer of the
      borough shall be eligible to serve on any board, commission, bureau or other agency
      created by or for the borough or any borough office created or authorized by statute
      and may accept appointments under the statute.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10A. Mayor›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A07. Duties of mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10A. Mayor › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A07. Duties of mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A07. Duties of mayor (2023)
content: The mayor shall have the following duties:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10A. Mayor›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A08. President or vice president of council to act as mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10A. Mayor › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A08. President or vice president of council to act as mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A08. President or vice president of council to act as mayor (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If the mayor is absent or incapacitated or there is a vacancy in the office, the duties
      of the office shall be discharged by the president of council or, in the absence or
      incapacity of the president of council or if there is a vacancy in the office, by
      the vice president of council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Accounts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Accounts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Accounts (2023)
content:
All officers and employees appointed by a council shall, if directed, render their
   accounts to the council for settlement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Bonds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Bonds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Bonds (2023)
content:
If an appointed officer or employee of a borough is required by law or action of council
   to give bond for the faithful performance of the officer's or employee's duties, the
   borough may pay the premium on the bond.  All bonds required to be given by borough officials or employees shall be with a
   surety company authorized by law to act as surety.  The borough shall pay a proportionate share of the cost of the bond of an appointed
   tax collector in the same ratio as provided in section 804 (relating to term and bonds)
   for elected tax collectors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1105. Compensation of certain employees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1105. Compensation of certain employees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1105. Compensation of certain employees (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A borough may provide, by ordinance, to appointees and employees of not less than
      ten years of satisfactory service and who are not less than 60 years of age upon termination
      of active employment with the borough, a proportion of the compensation last paid
      to them but not in excess of 50% of the compensation, including benefits received
      under the Social Security Act (49 Stat. 620,42 U.S.C. § 301 et seq.), if any, as fixed in the ordinance or amendment of the ordinance.

content:
(a) Required membership.--The following employees of municipal authorities shall be members of the borough retirement
      system upon a written election as provided in this section:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter B. Treasurer›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Bond and duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter B. Treasurer › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Bond and duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Bond and duties (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The borough treasurer shall, before entering upon the duties of office, give bond
      in an amount determined by council, conditioned for the faithful performance of the
      treasurer's duties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter D. Solicitor›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1118. Assistant solicitor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter D. Solicitor › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1118. Assistant solicitor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1118. Assistant solicitor (2023)
content:
A council may, by resolution, appoint an assistant solicitor to assist the solicitor
   in the performance of the solicitor's duties and, in the absence or disability of
   the solicitor, to perform the duties and exercise the powers of the solicitor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 10A. Mayor›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A01. Eligibility of mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 10A. Mayor › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A01. Eligibility of mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 10A01. Eligibility of mayor (2023)
content:
No mayor may hold any other borough office or appointment during the term for which
   the mayor is elected, except as is permitted under section 1104 (relating to appointments
   and incompatible offices).  The mayor shall be eligible to succeed himself.  The mayor shall not be a member of council, nor shall the mayor preside over or
   vote at any meeting of council, except as provided in section 1003 (relating to when
   the mayor may preside over council and vote, attendance of mayor at council meetings
   and breaking tie votes).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter E. Police›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1123. Police badge
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter E. Police › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1123. Police badge
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1123. Police badge (2023)
content:
Borough police officers shall wear a shield or badge with the word “Police” when on
   duty.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter E. Police›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1122. Police serving under cooperative agreement or contract
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter E. Police › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1122. Police serving under cooperative agreement or contract
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1122. Police serving under cooperative agreement or contract (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If a borough enters into a cooperative agreement or contract with any municipal corporation,
      regional police force or other governmental entity created by two or more municipal
      corporations under 53 Pa.C.S. Ch. 23 Subch. A (relating to intergovernmental cooperation) for the furnishing or receiving of police
      protection as authorized by section 1202(24) (relating to specific powers), the police
      force of the municipal corporation, regional police force or other governmental entity
      furnishing the police protection shall be appointed and accepted as the police force
      of the borough receiving the police service by resolution of the council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter B. Treasurer›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1107. Assistant treasurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter B. Treasurer › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1107. Assistant treasurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1107. Assistant treasurer (2023)
content:
A council may, by resolution, appoint an assistant treasurer who may not be a member
   of the council.  Council may appoint the assistant treasurer as the assistant secretary if the assistant
   treasurer is not a member of council.  The assistant treasurer shall assist the treasurer in the performance of the treasurer's
   duties and, in case of absence or disability of the treasurer, shall perform the duties
   and may exercise the powers of the treasurer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter D. Solicitor›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1116. Solicitor to have control of legal matters
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter D. Solicitor › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1116. Solicitor to have control of legal matters
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1116. Solicitor to have control of legal matters (2023)
content:
The legal matters of the borough shall be under the control of the borough solicitor.  No department or officer of the borough, except as otherwise provided by law, shall
   employ an additional counsel without the assent or ratification of the council.  The borough solicitor must be licensed to practice law in this Commonwealth and
   may be one person or a law firm, partnership, association or professional corporation.  The borough solicitor serves at the pleasure of council.  In the absence of the solicitor, the law firm of which the solicitor is a member
   or associate may perform any of the duties or functions of the solicitor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter C. Secretary›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1113. Records open to inspection
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter C. Secretary › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1113. Records open to inspection
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1113. Records open to inspection (2023)
content:
The fiscal records and documents and the minute book and other records and documents
   of every borough shall be open in accordance with the act of February 14, 2008 (P.L.
   6, No. 3),1known as the Right-to-Know Law.

content: (a) General rule.--The borough solicitor shall:

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter C. Secretary › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1111. Duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1111. Duties (2023)
content:
(a) Attendance at meetings and maintenance of minutes.--The secretary shall attend all meetings of the council and shall maintain full minutes
      of its proceedings.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter C. Secretary›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1112. Assistant secretary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter C. Secretary › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1112. Assistant secretary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1112. Assistant secretary (2023)
content:
A council may, by resolution, appoint an assistant secretary.  The assistant secretary shall assist the secretary in the performance of the secretary's
   duties and, in case of absence or disability of the secretary, perform the duties
   and may exercise the powers of the secretary.  The assistant secretary may be appointed from the membership of the council but
   shall not be any other officer of the council.  Council may appoint the assistant secretary as the assistant treasurer if the assistant
   secretary is not a member of council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter E. Police›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1125. Compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter E. Police › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1125. Compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1125. Compensation (2023)
content:
Borough police and special police appointed by the mayor shall receive compensation
   as fixed by the council.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter E. Police › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1123.1. Mayor's powers concerning police
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1123.1. Mayor's powers concerning police (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The mayor shall have full charge and control of the chief of police and the police
      force.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter E. Police › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1124. Suspension by mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1124. Suspension by mayor (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In addition to the powers of council to suspend police officers, the mayor may, for
      cause and without pay, suspend any police officers until the succeeding regular meeting
      of the council at which time or later the council may, subject to Subchapter J (relating
      to civil service for police and fire apparatus operators),1if they are in effect at the time, suspend, discharge, reduce in rank or reinstate
      with pay the police officers.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Private police pension funds and optional transfers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1132. Private police pension funds and optional transfers (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If there is a private organization or association constituting and managing an existing
      pension fund for the members of the police force in any borough, the borough shall
      establish a police pension for the purpose of paying pensions to the members of its
      police force if the membership of the organization or association by a two-thirds
      vote elects to transfer its funds with all its assets and liabilities into a borough
      pension fund as required to be established by this part.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1121. Council's powers concerning police (2023)
content: (a) Establishment of police department.--Council may, by ordinance, establish a police department.  If council establishes a police department, the following shall apply:

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter F. Police Pension Fund in Boroughs Having Police Force of Less Than Three Members › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1131. Police pension fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1131. Police pension fund (2023)
content:
(a) Authorization to establish.--If a police force of less than three full-time members is being maintained, the borough
      may, unless there is a private organization or association constituting and managing
      an existing pension fund for the members of the police force in the borough, by ordinance,
      establish a police pension fund into which each member of the police force shall pay
      an equal and proportionate monthly charge to be withheld from the pay of the member.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1172. Civil service commission

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1172. Civil service commission (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment.--A civil service commission is established in each borough where a police force or
      paid fire apparatus operators are maintained.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter G. Manager›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1143. Other offices not incompatible
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter G. Manager › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1143. Other offices not incompatible
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1143. Other offices not incompatible (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The offices of borough manager, street commissioner, secretary, treasurer and chief
      of police shall not be incompatible, and any two or more or all of the offices may
      be held by one person.  Neither the mayor nor any member of the council shall be eligible to hold the office
      of borough manager.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter G. Manager›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1141. Borough manager created by ordinance and election
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter G. Manager › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1141. Borough manager created by ordinance and election
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1141. Borough manager created by ordinance and election (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The council of a borough may, at its discretion at any time, create by ordinance the
      office of borough manager and may, in like manner, abolish the office. While the office exists, the council shall, from time to time, and if there is a vacancy,
      elect, by a vote of a majority of all the members, one individual, partnership, limited
      partnership, association or professional corporation as the borough manager.

content:
No commissioner shall at the same time hold an elective or appointed office under
   the Federal Government, this Commonwealth or any political subdivision of the Commonwealth,
   except that one member of the commission may be a member of the council and one may
   be a member of the teaching profession.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1176. Rules and regulations

content:
(a) General rule.--The commission may prescribe, amend and enforce rules and regulations for carrying
      into effect this subchapter and shall be governed by the rules and regulations.  Before the effective date of the rules and regulations or amendments to them, they
      shall be first approved by council.  If the rules and regulations or amendments have been approved, they shall not be
      annulled, amended or added to without the approval of council.

   and enforcement of this subchapter and rules and regulations adopted under this subchapter.  The chair of the commission may administer oaths and affirmations in connection
   with the investigations.

content:
(a) General rule.--The commission first appointed shall organize within ten days of its appointment and
      shall elect one of its members as the chair and one as the secretary.  Thereafter, the commission shall meet and organize within 30 days of the first Monday
      of each even-numbered year.  Each commissioner shall be notified in writing of each and every meeting.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1177. Minutes and records (2023)
content:
The commission shall maintain minutes of its proceedings and records of examinations
   and other official actions.  All recommendations of applicants for appointment received by the commission shall
   be kept and preserved for a period of five years, and all records and all written
   causes of removal filed with the commission, except as otherwise provided in section
   1191 (relating to hearings on dismissals and reductions), shall be open to public
   inspection and subject to reasonable regulation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1179. Subpoenas

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1179. Subpoenas (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The commission may issue subpoenas over the signature of the chair to require the
      attendance of witnesses and the production of records and papers pertaining to any
      investigation or inquiry.  The fees of witnesses for attendance and travel shall be the same as for witnesses
      appearing in the courts and shall be paid from appropriations for the incidental expenses
      of the commission.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1187. Provisional appointments

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1187. Provisional appointments (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If there are urgent reasons for the filling of a vacancy in a position in the police
      force and there are no names on the eligibility list for the appointment, the council
      may nominate a person to the commission for noncompetitive examination, and, if the
      nominee shall be certified by the commission as qualified after noncompetitive examination,
      the nominee may be appointed provisionally to fill the vacancy.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1185. Age and residency of applicants
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1185. Age and residency of applicants
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1185. Age and residency of applicants (2023)
content:
No person shall be eligible to apply for examination unless the person is at least
   18 years of age at the date of application.  An applicant need not be a resident of the borough.  The council of the borough may authorize the commission, by rule or regulation,
   to require police officers and paid fire apparatus operators to become residents of
   the borough after appointment to the positions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1188. Promotions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1188. Promotions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1188. Promotions (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A promotion shall be based on merit to be ascertained by an examination to be prescribed
      by the commission.  All questions relative to a promotion shall be practical in character and fairly
      test the merit and fitness of persons seeking promotion.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1186. Probationary period
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1186. Probationary period
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1186. Probationary period (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--An original appointment to a position in the police force or as a paid fire apparatus
      operator shall be for a probationary period of not less than six months and not more
      than one year, but during the probationary period an appointee may be dismissed only
      for a cause specified in section 1183 (relating to rejection of applicant and hearing)
      or because of incapacity for duty due to the use of alcohol or drugs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1180. Annual report

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1180. Annual report (2023)
content:
The commission shall make an annual report to the council containing a brief summary
   of its work during the year which shall be available for public inspection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter B. Treasurer›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1107. Assistant treasurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter B. Treasurer › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1107. Assistant treasurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1107. Assistant treasurer (2023)
content:
A council may, by resolution, appoint an assistant treasurer who may not be a member
   of the council.  Council may appoint the assistant treasurer as the assistant secretary if the assistant
   treasurer is not a member of council.  The assistant treasurer shall assist the treasurer in the performance of the treasurer's
   duties and, in case of absence or disability of the treasurer, shall perform the duties
   and may exercise the powers of the treasurer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Accounts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Accounts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Accounts (2023)
content:
All officers and employees appointed by a council shall, if directed, render their
   accounts to the council for settlement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Appointments and incompatible offices

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Appointments and incompatible offices (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Unless there is incompatibility in fact, an elective or appointive officer of the
      borough shall be eligible to serve on any board, commission, bureau or other agency
      created by or for the borough or any borough office created or authorized by statute
      and may accept appointments under the statute.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Compensation, hours and days of work and outside employment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Compensation, hours and days of work and outside employment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Compensation, hours and days of work and outside employment (2023)
content:
Appointed officers and employees of the borough shall receive compensation for their
   services as the council shall prescribe.  Council may also establish the hours and days of work and may restrict the outside
   employment of borough employees or any class or category of employment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Secretary›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1111. Duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Secretary › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1111. Duties

content:
(a) Attendance at meetings and maintenance of minutes.--The secretary shall attend all meetings of the council and shall maintain full minutes
      of its proceedings.

Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1193. Discrimination on account of political or religious affiliations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1193. Discrimination on account of political or religious affiliations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1193. Discrimination on account of political or religious affiliations (2023)
content:
(a) Information.--No question in any form of application for examination or in any examination shall
      be so framed as to elicit information concerning the political or religious opinions
      or affiliations of any applicant nor shall inquiry be made concerning the opinions
      or affiliations, and all disclosures of opinions or affiliations shall be ignored.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1191. Hearings on dismissals and reductions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1191. Hearings on dismissals and reductions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1191. Hearings on dismissals and reductions (2023)
content:
(a) Time of answer and hearing.--A person suspended, removed or reduced in rank may make written answers to any charges
      filed against the person not later than the day scheduled for the hearing.  The commission shall grant the person a hearing that shall be held within a period
      of ten days from the filing of written charges, unless continued by the commission
      for cause at the request of the council or the accused.  The failure of the commission to hold a hearing within ten days from the filing
      of the written charges shall not result in the dismissal of the charges filed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Bonds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Bonds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Bonds (2023)
content:
If an appointed officer or employee of a borough is required by law or action of council
   to give bond for the faithful performance of the officer's or employee's duties, the
   borough may pay the premium on the bond.  All bonds required to be given by borough officials or employees shall be with a
   surety company authorized by law to act as surety.  The borough shall pay a proportionate share of the cost of the bond of an appointed
   tax collector in the same ratio as provided in section 804 (relating to term and bonds)
   for elected tax collectors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter B. Treasurer›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Bond and duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter B. Treasurer › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Bond and duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Bond and duties (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The borough treasurer shall, before entering upon the duties of office, give bond
      in an amount determined by council, conditioned for the faithful performance of the
      treasurer's duties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Secretary›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1113. Records open to inspection
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Secretary › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1113. Records open to inspection
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1113. Records open to inspection (2023)
content:
The fiscal records and documents and the minute book and other records and documents
   of every borough shall be open in accordance with the act of February 14, 2008 (P.L.
   6, No. 3),1known as the Right-to-Know Law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter C. Secretary›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1112. Assistant secretary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter C. Secretary › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1112. Assistant secretary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1112. Assistant secretary (2023)
content:
A council may, by resolution, appoint an assistant secretary.  The assistant secretary shall assist the secretary in the performance of the secretary's
   duties and, in case of absence or disability of the secretary, perform the duties
   and may exercise the powers of the secretary.  The assistant secretary may be appointed from the membership of the council but
   shall not be any other officer of the council.  Council may appoint the assistant secretary as the assistant treasurer if the assistant
   secretary is not a member of council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1105. Compensation of certain employees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1105. Compensation of certain employees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1105. Compensation of certain employees (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A borough may provide, by ordinance, to appointees and employees of not less than
      ten years of satisfactory service and who are not less than 60 years of age upon termination
      of active employment with the borough, a proportion of the compensation last paid
      to them but not in excess of 50% of the compensation, including benefits received
      under the Social Security Act (49 Stat. 620,42 U.S.C. § 301 et seq.), if any, as fixed in the ordinance or amendment of the ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter D. Solicitor›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1116. Solicitor to have control of legal matters
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter D. Solicitor › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1116. Solicitor to have control of legal matters
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1116. Solicitor to have control of legal matters (2023)
content:
The legal matters of the borough shall be under the control of the borough solicitor.  No department or officer of the borough, except as otherwise provided by law, shall
   employ an additional counsel without the assent or ratification of the council.  The borough solicitor must be licensed to practice law in this Commonwealth and
   may be one person or a law firm, partnership, association or professional corporation.  The borough solicitor serves at the pleasure of council.  In the absence of the solicitor, the law firm of which the solicitor is a member
   or associate may perform any of the duties or functions of the solicitor.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1122. Police serving under cooperative agreement or contract (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If a borough enters into a cooperative agreement or contract with any municipal corporation,
      regional police force or other governmental entity created by two or more municipal
      corporations under 53 Pa.C.S. Ch. 23 Subch. A (relating to intergovernmental cooperation) for the furnishing or receiving of police
      protection as authorized by section 1202(24) (relating to specific powers), the police
      force of the municipal corporation, regional police force or other governmental entity
      furnishing the police protection shall be appointed and accepted as the police force
      of the borough receiving the police service by resolution of the council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1194. Penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 11. Powers, Duties and Rights of Appointed Officers and Employees › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1194. Penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1194. Penalty (2023)
content:
A member of council who, by vote, appoints any person to the police force or as a
   fire apparatus operator contrary to the provisions of this subchapter, or a member
   of council or member of the commission who willfully refuses to comply with or conform
   to the provisions of this subchapter, commits a misdemeanor and, upon conviction,
   shall be sentenced to pay a fine not exceeding $100 or to imprisonment not exceeding
   90 days, or both.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1192. Employees exempted (2023)
content:
All appointments in the police or fire forces of boroughs, including the chief of
   police or equivalent official, prior to the creation of a commission, shall continue
   to hold their positions and shall not be required to take any examination under the
   provisions of this subchapter, except that which may be required for promotion.  This section shall not be construed to apply to persons employed temporarily in
   emergency cases.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter D. Solicitor›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1118. Assistant solicitor

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1118. Assistant solicitor (2023)
content:
A council may, by resolution, appoint an assistant solicitor to assist the solicitor
   in the performance of the solicitor's duties and, in the absence or disability of
   the solicitor, to perform the duties and exercise the powers of the solicitor.

Borough police officers shall wear a shield or badge with the word “Police” when on

Borough police and special police appointed by the mayor shall receive compensation
   as fixed by the council.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter F. Police Pension Fund in Boroughs Having Police Force of Less Than Three Members › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1131. Police pension fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1131. Police pension fund (2023)
content:
(a) Authorization to establish.--If a police force of less than three full-time members is being maintained, the borough
      may, unless there is a private organization or association constituting and managing
      an existing pension fund for the members of the police force in the borough, by ordinance,
      establish a police pension fund into which each member of the police force shall pay
      an equal and proportionate monthly charge to be withheld from the pay of the member.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1123.1. Mayor's powers concerning police (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The mayor shall have full charge and control of the chief of police and the police
      force.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter E. Police › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1124. Suspension by mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1124. Suspension by mayor (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In addition to the powers of council to suspend police officers, the mayor may, for
      cause and without pay, suspend any police officers until the succeeding regular meeting
      of the council at which time or later the council may, subject to Subchapter J (relating
      to civil service for police and fire apparatus operators),1if they are in effect at the time, suspend, discharge, reduce in rank or reinstate
      with pay the police officers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter G. Manager›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1143. Other offices not incompatible
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter G. Manager › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1143. Other offices not incompatible
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1143. Other offices not incompatible (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The offices of borough manager, street commissioner, secretary, treasurer and chief
      of police shall not be incompatible, and any two or more or all of the offices may
      be held by one person.  Neither the mayor nor any member of the council shall be eligible to hold the office
      of borough manager.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter G. Manager›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1142. Powers and duties

content: (a) General rule.--The powers and duties of the borough manager shall be regulated by ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter G. Manager›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1141. Borough manager created by ordinance and election
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter G. Manager › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1141. Borough manager created by ordinance and election
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1141. Borough manager created by ordinance and election (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The council of a borough may, at its discretion at any time, create by ordinance the
      office of borough manager and may, in like manner, abolish the office. While the office exists, the council shall, from time to time, and if there is a vacancy,
      elect, by a vote of a majority of all the members, one individual, partnership, limited
      partnership, association or professional corporation as the borough manager.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1172. Civil service commission
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1172. Civil service commission
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1172. Civil service commission (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment.--A civil service commission is established in each borough where a police force or
      paid fire apparatus operators are maintained.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1174. Organization of commission
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1174. Organization of commission
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1174. Organization of commission (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The commission first appointed shall organize within ten days of its appointment and
      shall elect one of its members as the chair and one as the secretary.  Thereafter, the commission shall meet and organize within 30 days of the first Monday
      of each even-numbered year.  Each commissioner shall be notified in writing of each and every meeting.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter F. Police Pension Fund in Boroughs Having Police Force of Less Than Three Members›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1132. Private police pension funds and optional transfers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter F. Police Pension Fund in Boroughs Having Police Force of Less Than Three Members › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1132. Private police pension funds and optional transfers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1132. Private police pension funds and optional transfers (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If there is a private organization or association constituting and managing an existing
      pension fund for the members of the police force in any borough, the borough shall
      establish a police pension for the purpose of paying pensions to the members of its
      police force if the membership of the organization or association by a two-thirds
      vote elects to transfer its funds with all its assets and liabilities into a borough
      pension fund as required to be established by this part.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1176. Rules and regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1176. Rules and regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1176. Rules and regulations (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The commission may prescribe, amend and enforce rules and regulations for carrying
      into effect this subchapter and shall be governed by the rules and regulations.  Before the effective date of the rules and regulations or amendments to them, they
      shall be first approved by council.  If the rules and regulations or amendments have been approved, they shall not be
      annulled, amended or added to without the approval of council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1173. Offices incompatible with civil service commissioner
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1173. Offices incompatible with civil service commissioner
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1173. Offices incompatible with civil service commissioner (2023)
content:
No commissioner shall at the same time hold an elective or appointed office under
   the Federal Government, this Commonwealth or any political subdivision of the Commonwealth,
   except that one member of the commission may be a member of the council and one may
   be a member of the teaching profession.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1177. Minutes and records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1177. Minutes and records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1177. Minutes and records (2023)
content:
The commission shall maintain minutes of its proceedings and records of examinations
   and other official actions.  All recommendations of applicants for appointment received by the commission shall
   be kept and preserved for a period of five years, and all records and all written
   causes of removal filed with the commission, except as otherwise provided in section
   1191 (relating to hearings on dismissals and reductions), shall be open to public
   inspection and subject to reasonable regulation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1179. Subpoenas
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1179. Subpoenas
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1179. Subpoenas (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The commission may issue subpoenas over the signature of the chair to require the
      attendance of witnesses and the production of records and papers pertaining to any
      investigation or inquiry.  The fees of witnesses for attendance and travel shall be the same as for witnesses
      appearing in the courts and shall be paid from appropriations for the incidental expenses
      of the commission.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1180. Annual report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1180. Annual report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1180. Annual report (2023)
content:
The commission shall make an annual report to the council containing a brief summary
   of its work during the year which shall be available for public inspection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1186. Probationary period
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1186. Probationary period
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1186. Probationary period (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--An original appointment to a position in the police force or as a paid fire apparatus
      operator shall be for a probationary period of not less than six months and not more
      than one year, but during the probationary period an appointee may be dismissed only
      for a cause specified in section 1183 (relating to rejection of applicant and hearing)
      or because of incapacity for duty due to the use of alcohol or drugs.

      force and there are no names on the eligibility list for the appointment, the council
      may nominate a person to the commission for noncompetitive examination, and, if the
      nominee shall be certified by the commission as qualified after noncompetitive examination,
      the nominee may be appointed provisionally to fill the vacancy.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1192. Employees exempted
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1192. Employees exempted
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1192. Employees exempted (2023)
content:
All appointments in the police or fire forces of boroughs, including the chief of
   police or equivalent official, prior to the creation of a commission, shall continue
   to hold their positions and shall not be required to take any examination under the
   provisions of this subchapter, except that which may be required for promotion.  This section shall not be construed to apply to persons employed temporarily in
   emergency cases.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1185. Age and residency of applicants
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1185. Age and residency of applicants
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1185. Age and residency of applicants (2023)
content:
No person shall be eligible to apply for examination unless the person is at least
   18 years of age at the date of application.  An applicant need not be a resident of the borough.  The council of the borough may authorize the commission, by rule or regulation,
   to require police officers and paid fire apparatus operators to become residents of
   the borough after appointment to the positions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1191. Hearings on dismissals and reductions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1191. Hearings on dismissals and reductions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1191. Hearings on dismissals and reductions (2023)
content:
(a) Time of answer and hearing.--A person suspended, removed or reduced in rank may make written answers to any charges
      filed against the person not later than the day scheduled for the hearing.  The commission shall grant the person a hearing that shall be held within a period
      of ten days from the filing of written charges, unless continued by the commission
      for cause at the request of the council or the accused.  The failure of the commission to hold a hearing within ten days from the filing
      of the written charges shall not result in the dismissal of the charges filed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1190. Removals

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1190. Removals (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No person employed in any police or fire force of any borough may be suspended without
      pay, removed or reduced in rank except for the following reasons:

content: A borough may:

      and sale to the highest bidder shall apply if borough real or personal property is

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1188. Promotions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1188. Promotions (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A promotion shall be based on merit to be ascertained by an examination to be prescribed
      by the commission.  All questions relative to a promotion shall be practical in character and fairly
      test the merit and fitness of persons seeking promotion.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1194. Penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1194. Penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1194. Penalty (2023)
content:
A member of council who, by vote, appoints any person to the police force or as a
   fire apparatus operator contrary to the provisions of this subchapter, or a member
   of council or member of the commission who willfully refuses to comply with or conform
   to the provisions of this subchapter, commits a misdemeanor and, upon conviction,
   shall be sentenced to pay a fine not exceeding $100 or to imprisonment not exceeding
   90 days, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1193. Discrimination on account of political or religious affiliations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Subchapter J. Civil Service for Police and Fire Apparatus Operators › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1193. Discrimination on account of political or religious affiliations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1193. Discrimination on account of political or religious affiliations (2023)
content:
(a) Information.--No question in any form of application for examination or in any examination shall
      be so framed as to elicit information concerning the political or religious opinions
      or affiliations of any applicant nor shall inquiry be made concerning the opinions
      or affiliations, and all disclosures of opinions or affiliations shall be ignored.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 12. Corporate Powers›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1201.1. Real property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 12. Corporate Powers › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1201.1. Real property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1201.1. Real property (2023)
content:
(a) Sale.--No real estate owned by the borough may be sold except upon approval of council by
      resolution.  Additionally, no real estate owned by the borough may be sold for a consideration
      in excess of $6,000, except to the highest bidder after due notice by advertisement
      for bids or advertisement of a public auction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 12. Corporate Powers›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1201.2. Personal property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 12. Corporate Powers › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1201.2. Personal property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1201.2. Personal property (2023)
content:
(a) Sale.--Except as provided in subsection (b), no borough personal property may be disposed
      of, by sale or otherwise, except upon approval of council by resolution.  In cases when council approves a sale of the property, council shall estimate the
      fair market value of the entire lot to be disposed of.  If council estimates the fair market value to be $2,000 or more, the entire lot
      shall be advertised for sale once in at least one newspaper of general circulation
      not less than ten days prior to the date scheduled for the opening of bids or public
      auction.  The date of opening of bids or public auction shall be announced in the advertisement,
      and sale of the property advertised shall be made to the best responsible bidder.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns›Part I. Boroughs›Chapter 12. Corporate Powers›PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1203. Reserved powers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 8 Pa.C.S.A. Boroughs and Incorporated Towns › Part I. Boroughs › Chapter 12. Corporate Powers › PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1203. Reserved powers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 8 Pa.C.S.A. § 1203. Reserved powers (2023)
content:
The council may make and adopt all ordinances, bylaws, rules and regulations not inconsistent
   with or restrained by the Constitution of Pennsylvania and laws of this Commonwealth
   as may be expedient or necessary for the proper management, care and control of the
   borough and its finances and the maintenance of peace, good government, safety and
   welfare of the borough and its trade, commerce and manufactures.
